item.title: Title race wide open amid Bayern injuries and new-found Dortmund steel
item.description: Bayern Munich's Ismael Saibari goes down injured during the German Bundesliga soccer match between FC Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund at Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «Title race wide open amid Bayern injuries and new-found Dortmund steel») Sven Hoppe/dpa Borussia Dortmund battling back for a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich has spurred hope among their fans and many neutrals that this season's Bundesliga title race will be more memorable than the last. Bayern finished 16 points ahead of their main rivals as they sauntered to the championship last term. But their sudden raft of injuries and a more disciplined Dortmund under Niko Kovač suggest this campaign's title battle may be much closer. Substitute Fabio Silva grabbed Dortmund a point in the 89th minute on Saturday, meaning the big duo are locked on 18 points at the top of the table after eight games. Bayern are only top courtesy of their healthy goal difference. Home forwards Michael Olise, Serge Gnabry and Ismael Saibari all limped off the Allianz Arena turf on Saturday, with Morocco's Saibari looking particularly hurt with an ankle issue. “To be honest what's happening to us does feel a little heavy,” Bayern head of sport Max Eberl told reporters, referring to the injuries, coach Vincent Kompany's illness and Joshua Kimmich missing games due to the death of his father. "Right now we have to be very resilient." Bayern head to Atlético Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday and it seems unlikely Kompany will be back as he continues to recuperate from meningeal irritation. He has missed three games so far and assistant Aaron Danks is set to deputize again. Midfield general Kimmich was back against Dortmund but Manuel Neuer, Jamal Musiala and Luis Diaz were unavailable. Now Gnabry and Saibari could miss significant time, with Bayern's squad already stretched. "Both injuries are quite big," Eberl added without a full diagnosis. There was no word on wing wizard Olise. Plug the gaps Teenager Lennart Karl, criticized by club bosses in recent weeks amid a slump in form, will be expected to step up and help plug the gaps. Harry Kane, fresh from receiving the Ballon d'Or on Monday, was unusually wasteful against Dortmund and struck the bar with a penalty. While Bayern battle injuries, Dortmund have found a rare consistency this term having been labelled flaky by fans and pundits alike for years. “Of course, points in Munich aren’t a given - quite the opposite. So now we have one more point than we did last season,” ex-Bayern coach Kovač smirked, aware Dortmund lost both games against the Bavarians in 2025-26. “The team believed in themselves from the first minute to the last, fought hard, gave their all, and kept coming back even after falling behind twice. That shows the mentality the team has, as well as their strength and energy." item.title: European 1,500m champion Mageean dies aged 34
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Ireland's Ciara Mageean poses with her gold medal from the women's 1500 meters final of the European Athletics Championships. (is associated with: «European 1,500m champion Mageean dies aged 34») Michael Kappeler/dpa Ireland’s European 1,500 metres gold medallist Ciara Mageean has died at the age of 34 after suffering from cancer. Double Olympian Mageean, who won the European title in Rome in 2024, announced last year she had been diagnosed with bowel cancer. A statement on her Instagram account on Sunday read: “At 6:30am this morning, Ciara lost her battle with cancer surrounded by her loved ones. A beloved daughter, sister, wife, friend and inspiration to so many, she will be deeply missed.” Mageean, from Portaferry, County Down, in Northern Ireland, was married last month. Mageean, who competed at the Rio 2016 and Tokyo 2020 Olympics, also won European 1,500m silver in 2022 and bronze in 2016, while she finished fourth in the World Championships in 2023. She won silver competing for Northern Ireland at the Commonwealth Games in Birmingham in 2022. A statement from Athletics Ireland read: “Athletics Ireland is deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Ciara Mageean. “Ciara was a much-loved and inspirational figure who touched the lives of so many. Her courage, warmth and spirit will leave a lasting legacy. “The thoughts and heartfelt condolences of everyone at Athletics Ireland are with Ciara’s family, friends and loved ones at this incredibly difficult time. “May she rest in peace.”

item.title: Two-time Olympian Mageean dies aged 34
item.description: Mageean became a European champion in 2024 [Getty Images] Former European champion and two-time Olympian Ciara Mageean has died at the age of 34. Mageean, from Portaferry in Northern Ireland, was diagnosed with stage four bowel cancer in May 2025. She represented Ireland at the 2016 and 2020 Olympics, but was forced to withdraw from the 2024 Paris Games because of an Achilles injury. Earlier in 2024, Mageean had clinched the first major title of her career when she took 1500m gold at the European Championships in Rome. Prior to that she had also represented Northern Ireland at the Commonwealth Games, winning 1500m silver at Birmingham 2022. A statement posted on her social media on Sunday said: "At 6.30am this morning, Ciara lost her battle with cancer surrounded by her loved ones. "A beloved daughter, sister, wife, friend and inspiration to so many, she will be deeply missed. "Ar dheis Dé go raibh a hanam (may her soul rest in peace)." In a statement on social media, Athletics Ireland said: "We are heartbroken. An inspiration to so many, Ciara will be remembered for her courage, kindness and incredible spirit. "Our deepest sympathies are with her family, friends and loved ones at this difficult time. Rest in peace, Ciara." In October, Mageean wed her long-term partner Thomas Moran in a small civil ceremony in Belfast. A talented athlete from a young age, Mageean played camogie for Portaferry GAC, but her dream of representing Ireland at the Olympics led her to pursue a career in athletics. Her running prowess was clear during an impressive junior career that yielded 1500m silvers at the 2010 World Junior Championships and 2011 European Junior Championships. She also reached the 2010 Commonwealth Games 1500m final as an 18-year-old. However, Mageean's early progress in the senior ranks was hampered by a serious ankle injury, which ended her hopes of making her Olympic debut at London 2012. Having had surgery in 2013, Mageean won the Irish 1500m title on her return in July 2014. In 2016, she claimed 1500m bronze at the European Championships in Amsterdam, but her Olympic debut ended in disappointment as she exited the 1500m competition at the semi-final stage. In late 2017, Mageean left her Dublin base to join Steve Vernon's Team New Balance in Manchester after parting ways with coach Jerry Kiernan. item.title: Appreciating the career year Tee Higgins is having with the Bengals
item.description: When the Cincinnati Bengals drafted Tee Higgins in the second round of the 2020 Draft, it was a revival of something “cool” in Cincinnati. With their first two picks in that franchise-changing 2020 Draft, the Bengals selected Joe Burrow (No. 1 overall) and Tee Higgins (No. 33 overall). In doing so, they brought back a combination that took Cincinnati by storm 15 years prior; 9 + 85 = Cool. Carson Palmer and Chad Johnson made the Bengals cool in the mid-2000s. FOX19’s Jeremy Rauch did a story shortly after the 2020 Draft about how Burrow and Higgins would be bringing that cool combination back to The Jungle. Before the Bengals drafted Ja’Marr Chase the next year, with Chase now on his way towards becoming, arguably, the greatest wide receiver in Bengals history, it was Tee Higgins in the spotlight as Joe Burrow’s No. 1 wide receiver. The Bengals drafted Higgins to give Burrow a legitimate weapon to throw to, a rookie wide receiver to develop alongside Burrow in his rookie season. Burrow and Higgins quickly developed a strong connection, hooking up for four touchdowns and six straight games with Higgins going over 50 receiving yards. Higgins eclipsed 100 yards in two of those games. Six years later, and after five years of living in Ja’Marr Chase’s shadow, Tee Higgins is finally having a career year, his moment in the sun, you could say. But are we truly appreciating what Tee Higgins is doing through six games this season? He’s been playing like a WR1. Like a top 10 wide receiver in the NFL. Need proof? Higgins is currently No. 8 in the NFL with 571 receiving yards. In two of his last three games, Higgins has a combined 305 receiving yards. He has 266 receiving yards in his other four games, which is still a solid 66.5 receiving yards per game. Against Jacksonville in Week 4, Higgins was the Bengals’ best healthy wide receiver for three quarters. He caught 11 passes for 157 yards when the Jaguars’ defense knew the ball was going to him. Then against the Ravens, after being held without a catch in the first half, Higgins caught six passes for 148 yards and a touchdown in the second half. He took over the game, averaging 24.7 yards per reception and all six of his catches gaining a first down. There’s a reason Joe Burrow said Tee Higgins is a need back in 2024. Higgins can change any game with his vertical route running, big-play ability, and his knack for making chunk catches over the middle of the field. But he hasn’t been a streaky receiver this season. Higgins has 50+ receiving yards in five of the Bengals’ six games this season. In fact, he has over 90 receiving yards in four of his six games. Plus, he has five+ receptions in four of the Bengals’ six games. Higgins’ average of 95.2 receiving yards per game is by far his career-high. Prior to this season, it was 77.9 in 2021. item.title: Brooks Koepka may have now answered one of the key questions Bryson DeChambeau had about his future
item.description: Photo by Scott Taetsch/PGA of America via Getty Images Brooks Koepka could not resist a dig at Bryson DeChambeau during an interview this week, with the five-time major champion making fun of his old rival’s comments about Rory McIlroy from the 2025 Masters. Koepka and DeChambeau have had their issues over a number of years. It was clear that the two men were not particularly fond of each other, though they were eventually able to put those problems to one side ahead of the 2021 Ryder Cup at Whistling Straits. They also seemed to get along much better once they both moved to LIV Golf. However, Koepka went on to become the first big name to walk away from the league in late 2025. And it would appear that Koepka has made little attempt to stay in touch with DeChambeau now that he has moved back to the PGA Tour . Brooks Koepka’s dig may help explain why Bryson DeChambeau is ready to stay with LIV Golf Speaking to Dan Rapaport in an interview posted this week, Koepka joked that he can understand why no-one would want to speak to DeChambeau, when asked about the LIV star highlighting that Rory McIlroy did not talk to him during the final round of The Masters last year. Of course, McIlroy himself made his feelings about DeChambeau known at The Open Championship this year, with the Northern Irishman admitting he is not a fan of the two-time US Open champion. The digs from the likes of Koepka and McIlroy perhaps highlight one of the reasons DeChambeau looks set to stay with LIV Golf beyond this year given what he previously said about a PGA Tour return. In an interview with Skratch in May, DeChambeau noted that he would only be interested in coming back to the PGA Tour if the membership wanted him back. Koepka and McIlroy do not speak for the rest of the players, obviously. However, they are extremely influential. No active player on the PGA Tour can compete with the pair for major victories, so their comments are significant. Bryson DeChambeau is clearly reluctant to be the PGA Tour’s pantomime villain again DeChambeau has become accustomed to being the superstar of his league. On LIV, he was the biggest name. He was the player that many fans came to see. And the other players seemed to be very happy to protect him when he would face any criticism or ridicule from the outside. He would clearly have plenty of friends if he returned to the PGA Tour. DeChambeau was praised whenever his teammates had an opportunity to talk about him during the 2025 Ryder Cup at Bethpage. However, DeChambeau is loved and idolised on LIV. He is obviously aware that he would be considered a much more divisive character if he returned to the PGA Tour, and does not have the desire to take on that particular challenge.

item.title: Former France star slams Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe over Ballon d’Or campaign: ‘He lost control’
item.description: Former France star slams Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe over Ballon d’Or campaign: ‘He lost control’ Real Madrid firmly believed that their superstar attacker, Kylian Mbappe, had a chance to win the 2026 Ballon d’Or in London last Monday. However, the Frenchman lost out to Harry Kane , with the Bayern Munich striker lifting the prestigious individual accolade. Mbappe finished just 28 points behind the Englishman, the narrowest margin by which a player has lost the award. Meanwhile, the Frenchman has been receiving some criticism over the manner in which he promoted his individual achievements. Lizarazu questions Mbappe’s attitude Former France international Bixente Lizarazu did not hold back when discussing the Real Madrid superstar. Speaking to Franceinfo after the ceremony, he questioned Mbappe’s attitude towards putting himself ahead of the team. “I defended Mbappe a lot last season, when he was still being heavily criticised from all sides,” Lizarazu said (h/t RM4Arab ). Kylian Mbappe has copped some flak for his actions before the Ballon d’Or. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) “He had a good World Cup, and I thought he was consistent in his role as France captain, with a message focused on teamwork. But during the Ballon d’Or campaign, he completely lost control.” “I didn’t like the direction he took at all. He became too focused on individual matters, showed a lack of humility and engaged in self-promotion, somewhat ignoring the others.” The former defender added: “We were left with the impression that he was the only one who mattered, as though the others didn’t exist.” Lizarazu believes goals are not enough Lizarazu also questioned why Mbappe’s individual numbers had not translated into collective success for his team. “Kylian Mbappe has gone through periods when he hasn’t managed to make his team win,” he argued . Mbappe will hope to win the Ballon d’Or next year. (Photo by Aurelien Meunier/Getty Images) “He scores a lot of goals, but he has to make his team win. That is the most important thing.” This was one of the major factors that eventually worked against the Frenchman in the final Ballon d’Or results. For all of Mbappe’s impressive numbers last season, he was not able to win a single piece of silverware for either club or country. However, blaming one individual for a team’s failure to win trophies would be equally unfair. Mbappe did everything he could. His brace against Barcelona is the perfect example of how Mbappe steps up in big games more often than not. Under Jose Mourinho, Madrid also seem to be building the team around Mbappe to help bring trophies back to the Bernabeu . If Mbappe goes on to have a similar season to last year and also lifts trophies, no one can stop him from winning the Ballon d’Or in 2027.

(Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) Getty Images In just their second year of existence, the Golden State Valkyries won the 2026 WNBA championship. The Valkyries toppled Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream in a hard-fought, seven-game series that ended in " Ballhalla " on Halloween. The Valkyries made history by winning a title that quickly. Prior to their victory, the Milwaukee Bucks had the record for the quickest championship by an expansion team, but it took them three years to win theirs. Golden State can chalk up its unprecedented success to a few different factors. But as the NBA weighs whether to add expansion teams in Las Vegas, Seattle or both cities in the coming years, it can and should look to what the Valkyries accomplished as a template to follow, particularly given the expected price tag of its expansion teams. What The Valkyries Got Right To some extent, the Valkyries lucked out with their timing. They were the only expansion team joining the WNBA in 2025—compared to 2026, when both the Toronto Tempo and Portland Fire came online—which means they faced zero competition for selections in the 2024 expansion draft . Most of the players whom the Valkyries selected in that expansion draft are no longer with the team, even though it’s been less than two years since that draft was held. However, they did land Veronica Burton, Cecilia Zandalasini and Kayla Thornton in the expansion draft, all of whom had their moments throughout their run to the championship this year. They rounded out their starting five by signing Kaila Charles, Kiah Stokes and Gabby Williams—who went on to win 2026 Finals MVP—in free agency this year. The Williams signing in particular proved to be franchise-changing, as she went on to average a career-high 14.4 points per game during the regular season this year. item.title: Harriet Dart wins first WTA title with Guangzhou Open fightback
item.description: Britain’s Harriet Dart won her first WTA title after coming from a set down to beat Lilli Tagger in the final of the Guangzhou Open in China. Dart, who saved three match points in her semi-final win over Sun Xinran to reach her first Tour-level final, edged a thrilling match against the 18-year-old from Austria 4-6 6-3 6-4. Qualifier Dart, the British number five, dropped serve in the opening game and had to save a break point in her next service game before finally getting on the board. The 30-year-old from Hampstead broke back for 4-4, but Tagger hit straight back before wrapping up the first set. The first break point of the second set came the way of Dart, who took it for 5-3 on her way to levelling the match. In a tense deciding set, a run of five consecutive breaks of serve ended when gutsy Dart saved two break points to hold for 5-3. In the next she brought up two championship points, but a big Tagger serve saved the first before Dart netted a mid-court forehand on the second. However, Dart wiped that miss from her mind to serve out the match to 15, falling on her back in delight when victory was sealed with an unreturned serve. item.description: Liam Lawson apologized to Max Verstappen for their Mexico GP practice clash, then was disqualified from qualifying over a separate MGU-K rules breach. It was an unnecessary situation in FP2 when Racing Bulls’ Lawson and Red Bull’s Verstappen came together at the end of the lap. And obviously tomorrow is a long race. I think when you come in from a session, obviously I didn’t talk to the media yesterday, so yeah, when you come in from a session, and there’s adrenaline, ultimately only Max knows how he feels. “So, yeah, obviously, as I said, it was never my intention to have contact, so apologies for that,” Lawson said. item.title: Wednesday appoint former Stockport boss Challinor
item.description: Dave Challinor previously worked with Sheffield Wednesday's sporting director Simon Wilson at Stockport County [Shutterstock] Sheffield Wednesday have appointed former Stockport County boss Dave Challinor as their new manager. He replaces Henrik Pedersen, who was sacked last Sunday after just one win in six League One games. The Owls are currently on a winless run of three matches - where they have drawn once and lost twice - and are ninth in the table. They next play Blackpool at 14:00 GMT on Sunday, for which Challinor will be watching from the stands as interim boss Matt Hamshaw takes charge. A former Bury and Tranmere Rovers defender, Challinor began his managerial career at Colwyn Bay in 2010. The 51-year-old has since achieved multiple promotions across spells with AFC Fylde and Hartlepool. More recently, he guided Stockport County from the National League and to the League Two title within three seasons - and twice took them to the League One play-offs. The Englishman departed the Hatters by mutual consent at the conclusion of the 2025-26 season after losing in the play-off final to Bolton Wanderers. 'Challinor fits the bill' - analysis BBC Radio Sheffield's Rob Staton Sheffield Wednesday's new owners wanted to bring in a winner - someone capable of turning recent defeats and draws into victories. Challinor's record fits the bill, with seven promotions to his name already. He also knows League One through his time at Stockport County. His task will be to provide an effective form of football. He has to bring a Sheffield Wednesday squad together that has talented individuals but now needs to be shaped into a team. The top seven in League One is starting to look strong and Wednesday, along with Leicester and possibly the rising MK Dons, will be looking at joining the group that appears to be establishing. This will be an interesting next step for Challinor. It's a very different job to Stockport, Hartlepool or Fylde - with massive expectations. Whenever Wednesday are in League One, you're expected to win. A lot. Darren Moore had a 96-point season at this level and was always only a bad result away from having people question his job. I'd expect he will probably be joined by Clint Hill and Anthony Sweeney on his staff. Simon Wilson, who worked with Challinor at Stockport, will have been instrumental in the appointment.
